sources.description: Moku (Historic Land Divisions), including names with diacritical marks. Source: State Historic Preservation Division (SHPD), December 2020. Derived by dissolving ahupuaa boundaries on moku name. See also ahupuaa GIS layer. July 2026: Updates were made by State Historic Preservation Division (SHPD) to the moku and ahupuaʻa layers for a section of east Oʻahu, based upon supporting documentation received by SHPD. Maunalua and Kuliʻouʻou are now within the moku of Kona. Previously they were within the moku of Koʻolaupoko and considered a part of Waimānalo. See full metadata for more information.For additional information, please refer to complete metadata at https://files.hawaii.gov/dbedt/op/gis/data/moku.pdf or contact Hawaii Statewide GIS Program, Office of Planning and Sustainable Development, State of Hawaii; PO Box 2359, Honolulu, HI 96804; (808) 587-2846; email: gis@hawaii.gov; Website: https://planning.hawaii.gov/gis.

processing: Fetched from the ArcGIS REST service as GeoJSON in WGS84 (outSR=4326). Coordinates snapped to 1e-6 degrees, then simplified together with the other boundary file (shared arcs, Douglas–Peucker, 50 m tolerance in the projection of manifest.json, finer where needed to keep rings valid). Winding per RFC 7946. Added properties: name, island, islandId, mokuKey, gisId, with the standard ʻokina (U+02BB) and kahakō in name and island; every other property is the layer's own, verbatim.
